paper.title: The End of Optimism? An Asymptotic Analysis of Finite-Armed Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-armed stochastic linear bandit with Gaussian noise
unmapped: actions have Euclidean norm at most 1
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal A \subset \R^d$ be a finite set that spans $\R^d$ with $|\mathcal A| = k$ and $\norm{x}_2 \leq 1$ for all $x \in \cA$. A learner interacts with the bandit over $n$ rounds. In each round $t$ the learner chooses an action (arm) $A_t \in \mathcal A$ and observes a payoff $Y_t = \inner{A_t, \theta} + \eta_t$ where $\eta_t \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-armed stochastic linear bandit with Gaussian noise (lower bound)
unmapped: actions have Euclidean norm at most 1
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal A \subset \R^d$ be a finite set that spans $\R^d$ with $|\mathcal A| = k$ and $\norm{x}_2 \leq 1$ for all $x \in \cA$. ... observes a payoff $Y_t = \inner{A_t, \theta} + \eta_t$ where $\eta_t \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$

symbols.C_lin: c(A, theta): value of inf_alpha sum_{x suboptimal} alpha(x) Delta_x s.t. ||x||^2_{H(alpha)^{-1}} <= Delta_x^2/2 for all suboptimal x, H(alpha)=sum alpha(x) x x^T

conditions: Gram matrix bar G_n eventually invertible (shown to hold for consistent policies in appendix)

source.label: cor:regretlb
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be a consistent policy, $\theta\in \R^d$ such that there is a unique optimal arm in $\cA$. Then $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \log(n) \norm{x}_{\bar G_n^{-1}}^2 \leq \frac{\Delta_x^2}{2}$ and also $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{R_\theta^\pi(n)}{\log(n)} \geq c(\mathcal A, \theta)$, where $c(\mathcal A, \theta)$ is defined as the solution to the following optimisation problem...

results.notes: Derived from Theorem 1 (allocation constraint limsup log(n)||x-x*||^2_{G_n^{-1}} <= Delta_x^2/2 for consistent policies), which is not recorded separately as it is not directly a regret bound. Appendix proof actually gives the stronger liminf version. For standard basis action sets, c(A,theta)=sum 2/Delta_x (Lai-Robbins, Example 3).

symbols.C_lin: c(A, theta): value of the optimisation problem in Corollary 2

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Assuming that $x^*$ is unique, the strategy given in Algorithm \ref{alg:optimal} satisfies \limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi_\theta(n)}{\log(n)} \leq c(\mathcal A, \theta) for all \theta \in \R^d.

results.notes: Algorithm takes A and n as input (known horizon). Matches the lower bound of Corollary 2. Paper says Gaussian assumption can be relaxed to 1-subgaussian for the upper bound. Algorithm solves an optimisation problem per run; computational cost not stated.
